songs.name: And We Bid You Good Night

ai_show_review.summary: Scorching Dark Star, monumental Other One, tight Caution‑Feedback
ai_show_review.blurb: The show erupts with a blistering Dark Star and an epic Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One sequence. Jerry’s guitar is on fire while Phil locks in off‑the‑charts bass interplay. A soaring second half delivers a powerful Caution → Feedback → Good Night finish despite mid‑set tape dip.
ai_show_review.review: On November 1, 1968 at the Silver Dollar Fairgrounds, the Dead unleashed one of their most ferocious early‑season performances. The set opens with a searing Dark Star that showcases Garcia’s soaring tone and fearless improvisation, then rolls into a double‑take Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One sandwich where Jerry and Phil push each other to new heights. After the brief stumble of New Potato Caboose—where the tape begins to sag—the band rebounds spectacularly: The Other One reaches monumental intensity, and the closing Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) → Feedback → And We Bid You Good Night sequence adds relentless momentum. Across all seven soundboard sources the playing is consistently praised; the only recurring grievance is Bob’s rhythm guitar being buried after the mid‑set dip. For listeners seeking the definitive version of this scorching show, the Kaplan SBD (gd1968-11-01.sbd.kaplan.17080.sbeok.shnf) offers sublime early clarity and captures the fire that defines this night.

best_recording.reason: Provides the clearest early capture of the set and preserves the fire of the performance despite mid‑set tape dip.

key_highlights: Monumental The Other One with ferocious Garcia‑Lesh interplay.
Scorching Dark Star opening that showcases Jerry’s soaring tone.
Tight Caution → Feedback → Good Night sequence that builds unstoppable momentum.
Early recording quality is excellent; after New Potato the mix drops and Bob’s guitar is buried.
song_highlights: And We Bid You Good Night

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia is on fire—ferocious tone and dominant lead work that drives the Dark Star and makes The Other One monumental.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh delivers off‑the‑charts interplay with Garcia, especially during The Other One, providing a solid, creative bass foundation.
band_performance.Bob: Weir’s rhythm guitar is often buried in the mix after New Potato, but his vocals are excited and cut through when heard.
